title: The Fortunate King
tagline: The sea answered his call, and the world opened before him.

scenes.text: Lisbon, 1495. Manuel inherits the Portuguese crown — and with it, the most advanced maritime programme in the world. Decades of exploration have mapped the coast of Africa. Now the route to India beckons. Manuel sees not just trade routes but destiny.

scenes.speaker: Manuel I of Portugal
scenes.text: The wealth of the East passes through Arab and Venetian hands before it reaches us. What if it came directly? What if Lisbon became the hub of the world's trade?

challenge.instruction: Manuel's council warns that a fleet to India will ruin the kingdom. Win the court round, faction by faction, before the ships can sail.
challenge.fact: 'Manuel, o Venturoso' — The Fortunate. Under his reign, Vasco da Gama reached India (1498), Pedro Cabral reached Brazil (1500), and Portugal controlled the world's spice trade. Lisbon became the richest city in Europe.

scenes.text: He commissioned Vasco da Gama to sail around Africa to India. In 1498, da Gama arrived at Calicut. The spice route was open. Manuel's Portugal was suddenly the richest nation in Europe, with trading posts from Brazil to Japan.

scenes.speaker: Vasco da Gama
scenes.text: The Indians have their own merchants, their own navies, their own trade. They did not expect us. Some welcomed us. Others did not.

scenes.speaker: Manuel I of Portugal
scenes.text: Then we must be the ones who make our welcome unavoidable. Build a fortress. Establish trade. The sea route must remain ours.

challenge.instruction: Calicut's ruler will not let the newcomers stay. Hold the fords of Cochin, Portugal's only ally, with a handful of men against his army.
challenge.fact: Vasco da Gama's first voyage of 1497–99 lost two of its four ships and more than half its men, but the spices it brought home paid for it many times over. Manuel answered Calicut's hostility with armed fleets every year and a chain of forts.

scenes.text: Under Manuel, Portugal controlled the entire Eastern spice trade. Albuquerque conquered Goa, Malacca, Hormuz. Cabral claimed Brazil. The small nation on Europe's western edge became the first global empire. They called Manuel 'O Venturoso' — the Fortunate.

scenes.speaker: Manuel I of Portugal
scenes.text: Some kings are remembered for their battles. I will be remembered for the oceans my people crossed and the worlds they found.

challenge.instruction: With Goa, Malacca and Hormuz in Portuguese hands, the riches of the East come up the Tagus. Reckon each cargo into the king's ledger as the clerk calls it.
challenge.fact: Albuquerque took Goa in 1510, Malacca in 1511 and Hormuz in 1515, giving Portugal command of the straits of the Indian Ocean. For a generation Lisbon set the price of pepper for all of Europe.

challenge.instruction: From Lisbon to Malacca, Manuel's forts ring the Indian Ocean, and in their shadow life goes on. Sit down at the board with a merchant of Kilwa.
challenge.fact: Manuel's reign gave its name to the Manueline style, whose stone ropes, armillary spheres and sea creatures cover the Jerónimos Monastery and the Tower of Belém in Lisbon, both built with the profits of the spice trade.

challenge.instruction: Not all of Manuel's fortune comes from the East: Madeira's sugar mills grind for the crown too. Build the gear train so the water wheel turns the crushing stone just right.
challenge.fact: Madeira, settled by the Portuguese from the 1420s, was Europe's great source of sugar by 1500. The planters' methods were carried on to São Tomé and then to Brazil, the land Cabral claimed for Manuel in 1500.

scenes.speaker: Manuel I of Portugal
scenes.text: Qusqu is under Depression. At the end of every round, any side whose Wealth totals under 5 is swept from the board. Alan Turing is already there and far too weak to last. Put me there and hold.

challenge.instruction: Fight lesson 4 · Survival. Deploy Manuel I of Portugal to Qusqu, keep at least 5 Wealth there, and End Turn until two round endings have passed.
challenge.fact: A Local Survival event is a test, not a fight: at the end of each round every side at the location is checked, and a total under 5 loses every card there to the discard pile. Reinforce with followers, or retrieve a weak card before the round ends.
